document.intro: A real notice from the University of Salzburg, in German and English, from the Covid years. It’s useful, because of one German structure: *ist … zu tragen*. A rule, in the zu + verb you’ve just learned.
document.fact: When rules are written in *ist … zu …*, they’re meant seriously: *Die Tür ist zu schließen*, the door must be closed. It’s the voice of notices, contracts and exam papers, and it tells you that no one wrote this with love.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Turn each rule into a sentence with zu: Es ist wichtig, … zu …
reading.title: Ich habe vor, anzufangen
reading.intro: Jonas from Freiburg has been a student for fourteen semesters. His subject has changed three times. Now he has moved to Göttingen, where his friend Paula is about to get her doctorate. She has found him in the Mensa, and she’s asked him what he is actually doing.
reading.photos[1].caption: Das Gänseliesel: das meistgeküsste Mädchen der Welt.
reading.fact: The Gänseliesel in Göttingen is said to be the most-kissed girl in the world. New doctors get a *Doktorwagen*, a decorated cart pulled by their friends, and a hat made by friends too. A 1926 ban on kissing her has been cheerfully ignored ever since.
